title: GenEDA: Towards Generative Netlist Functional Reasoning via Cross-Modal Circuit Encoder-Decoder Alignment
problem: Existing circuit foundation models are limited to standalone encoders or decoders, operating on different circuit modalities and separate latent spaces, preventing complementary capability development.
motivation: Foundation models tailored for IC design can accelerate automation if they unify multiple modalities and reasoning capabilities.
method: GenEDA presents first framework cross-modally aligning circuit encoders with decoders in shared latent space, bridging graph-based circuit representation learning and text-based LLMs. Provides two paradigms supporting both trainable and frozen commercial LLMs.
key_novelty: Cross-modal encoder-decoder alignment enabling LLMs to directly reason over low-level bit-blasted netlists and generate high-level specifications.
contributions: First cross-modal encoder-decoder alignment framework for circuits
Shared latent space bridging graph and text modalities
Support for both trainable and frozen commercial LLMs
First generative foundation model for netlists enabling netlist-to-spec generation
Significant performance boost on LLMs (GPT, DeepSeek) for functional reasoning tasks

metrics.accuracy: Significant performance boost on advanced LLMs

limitations: Evaluation on specific netlist-to-spec tasks; generalization to other circuit reasoning tasks and very large designs not explored.
